findings.title: Phishing kits adapt to the script of callers
findings.summary_md: Okta Threat Intelligence dissected multiple custom phishing kits offered as a service and built for voice-based social engineers. The kits let a caller change what a victim sees in the browser in sync with the call, intercept credentials and manipulate MFA prompts, and were used against Google, Microsoft, Okta and cryptocurrency providers. Okta said this synchronization defeats any MFA that is not phishing-resistant and published a customer-only advisory with details of two kits.

findings.title: Special Alert: SLSH Malicious Supergroup Targeting 100+ Organizations via Live Phishing Panels
findings.summary_md: Silent Push warned that more than 100 high-value enterprises were being targeted through Okta SSO and other SSO platforms using live phishing panels. It attributed the infrastructure to SLSH, an alliance of Scattered Spider, LAPSUS$ and ShinyHunters, and described a human-led vishing operation that intercepts credentials and MFA tokens in real time. The published target list spanned technology, fintech, biotech, banking and real estate firms, including Atlassian, Canva, Epic Games, Moderna and State Street.

findings.title: Former ShinyHunters Cluster Moves to New INCEPTION Site
findings.summary_md: Okta assessed that organizations targeted by O-UNC-053 began appearing on a new INCEPTION data leak site in November 2026 instead of the ShinyHunters site that published targets from March through September. The cluster, active since March, uses vishing to harvest credentials and MFA factors, and Okta said its kit cannot defeat FastPass or FIDO2/WebAuthn passkeys. Domain registrations for the legal-themed campaign began in late October, with INCEPTION listings six to 19 days after related infrastructure was registered. Okta said the cluster very likely changed brand affiliation but could not assess with high confidence whether it runs the new site or partners with another extortion actor.

findings.title: Threat Researcher's Notebook: SSO Vishing Campaign Associated with Emerging Inception Extortion Group
findings.summary_md: ReversingLabs tied the SSO vishing campaign to INCEPTION's Tor leak site, which indexed five claimed victims on November 17 and later added AutoZone and Lucid Motors for seven total. It confirmed 21 domains serving the SSO phishing kit, attributed 41 more at high confidence and four at medium confidence, and found the lure domains had no MX, DKIM or DMARC records, indicating phone-led delivery that bypasses email controls. The kit redirected unexpected visitors to legitimate Okta or NetIQ sign-in pages, and staging indicators included NICENIC registrations, Cloudflare nameservers and evening UTC registration windows. ReversingLabs advised hunting DNS, proxy and identity-provider logs from October 21, 2026 onward.

findings.title: Inception, possibly a ShinyHunters reboot, claims seven victims in a week
findings.summary_md: The Register reported Okta's assessment that O-UNC-053 had very likely changed brand affiliation from ShinyHunters to INCEPTION while keeping the same vishing and domain-registration tactics. The first five claimed victims, AMD, Cigna Healthcare, Paychex, PepsiCo and Henry Schein, were listed as leaked on November 17, followed by AutoZone on November 19 and Lucid Group on November 21. None of the seven confirmed a breach, and Okta said it could not validate the published data. The piece placed the cluster in the wider Com ecosystem and noted that infrastructure was registered six to 19 days before each company appeared on the new leak site.
